proposals.evidence: DEDR 5401 gives Kolami vitanam, Kota vit, Malayalam vittu/vita/vitar, Parji vittid, Tamil vitai, Telugu vittanamu and Toda pït in the seed/sowing family. Source annotations independently identify the article. Survey Tamil vedə and Toda pittə remain comparative spelling/ending variants. The possible Indo-Aryan bīj-/bic- seed responses are excluded from this proposal. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 3559 gives the tōl/tokku skin/bark family with Gondi tōla bark, Kodagu tōlï skin, Gadaba tōl skin/bark, Tamil tōl skin and Toda twï·s̱ skin. Source cognacy explicitly identifies the article. Betta Kurumba tōlə is a comparative extension noted as a look-alike by the source; Gadaba tal and Toda tūrs preserve their survey vowel/consonant differences. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 561 documents Kannada ugur, Kodagu oy, Gondi gōr, Kurukh orox, Kuwi gōru with plural gōrka, Malto orgu and Toda ǖr as the nail/claw family. Survey final vowels and plural-looking material remain unchanged. Badaga ugilə is a comparative extension explicitly described as a look-alike in the source; Kodagu voyi and Toda yūr retain their initial glide/transcription differences. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 3986(a) documents the pal tooth family: Kodagu pallï, Malayalam pallu, Tamil pal, Malto palu, Kolami pal, Gadaba pal/pallū with plural palkīl, and Toda pas̱. Survey plural and final-vowel material (including palku, pālkill, pāldu) remains unchanged. Toda parse is a comparative correspondence to its distinctive s̱ reflex; Betta Kurumba pallə extends the comparison to a lect absent from this article. Subsection (b) toothstick compounds are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 474 explicitly documents Kannada eraḍu, Kodagu daṇḍï, Kota eyḏ, Kurukh irb (two persons), Kuwi rindi, Malayalam raṇṭu, Parji adjectival ir, Tamil reṇṭu and Toda ēḍ. The survey cognacy annotations independently identify the article. Final vowels and the Kurukh personal versus Parji adjectival use are retained; no grammatical category is silently added to the generic survey gloss two. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
